item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Putin’s 2023 record is strongly negative on 7B.9. The clearest pattern is favoritism and transactional control through loyalist appointments, secrecy around officials’ finances, pressure on independent media/monitors, and coercive treatment of firms and critics. The pro-side evidence is narrow and mostly technocratic: some universal social payments and isolated professional pushback inside economic policy.

**Accepted Claims**

- **[Putin ally appointed to head Russia’s TASS news agency](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-ally-appointed-to-head-russias-tass-news-agency-3073207)** | *Reuters* | May 7, 2023 | Putin’s former election spokesman Andrei Kondrashov was appointed to run TASS. That is direct patronage in a major public-information institution, not merit-neutral staffing. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5, 7B.6

- **[Russian MPs vote to hide tax returns from public view](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jan/25/russian-mps-vote-to-hide-details-of-their-tax-returns-from-public-view)** | *The Guardian / AFP* | Jan. 25, 2023 | The State Duma voted to anonymize lawmakers’ tax and asset reports, reducing public transparency around conflicts of interest and hidden enrichment. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.8

- **[Russia’s new foreign-agent restrictions](https://tass.com/politics/1480071)** | *TASS* | Jul. 14, 2022, but the law remained operative in 2023 and was expanded further | Putin signed a law broadening “foreign agent” designations to people under foreign influence and those collecting military-related information. In 2023 this logic continued to suppress critics and treat information control as a political loyalty test. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.8

- **[Russia is preparing a “loyalty agreement” requirement for foreigners](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/draft-bill-seeks-loyalty-agreement-from-foreigners-entering-russia-3252165)** | *Reuters* | Nov. 29, 2023 | The draft would force foreigners to promise not to criticize official policy or violate approved narratives. That is overt transactional politics around access and speech, not impartial administration. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.8

- **[Putin signs decree taking over Russian assets of two foreign firms](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-signs-decree-taking-over-russian-assets-of-two-foreign-firms-3064283)** | *Reuters* | Apr. 25, 2023 | Putin imposed temporary state control over Fortum and Uniper assets, explicitly as retaliation for foreign moves against Russian companies. That is politicized expropriation, not neutral enforcement. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.8**

- **[Factbox: Moscow takes control over assets of Western companies](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxmoscow-takes-control-over-assets-of-western-companies-3136331)** | *Reuters* | Jul. 27, 2023 | Reuters documented a broader pattern of state takeovers of Western firms’ Russian assets, including Carlsberg, Danone, Fortum, and Uniper. This reinforces that enforcement and property control were being used transactionally. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.8

- **[Putin tells Russia’s billionaires to put patriotism before profit](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/putin-urges-russias-billionaires-to-invest-in-face-of-sanctions-war-3032372)** | *Reuters* | Mar. 16, 2023 | Putin told oligarchs their role was not just to make money but to support society and the state. That is loyalty framing, not a clean separation of business from political favor. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5

- **[Putin’s social-benefits package](https://government.ru/en/news/47503/)** | *Government of the Russian Federation* | Jan. 9, 2023 | The government expanded free medical care, rehabilitation, child benefits, and special payments for medical workers through standardized administrative channels. This is the strongest narrow counterexample: some public benefits were rule-based rather than blatantly clientelist. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5

- **[Child payments centralized onto a fixed delivery date](https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2023/01/25/250437)** | *Social Fund of Russia* | Jan. 25, 2023 | Child payments were standardized onto a common delivery date, reducing ad hoc discretion. This is limited evidence of non-clientelist administration, but it does not offset the broader patronage pattern. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5

- **[Nabiullina resists arbitrary seizure of foreign bank units](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russia-should-not-take-temporary-control-of-foreign-banks-units-central-bank-3067714)** | *Reuters* | Apr. 28, 2023 | Central Bank head Elvira Nabiullina publicly opposed a more arbitrary seizure of foreign bank units. This shows narrow technocratic restraint inside the system, but not a general anti-favoritism rule. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5

- **[Putin convened government and Central Bank on development goals](https://www.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/70364)** | *Kremlin* | Jan. 17, 2023 | Putin kept the government and Central Bank in the core economic decision loop and discussed “concrete measures.” This is weak pro-side evidence for technocratic process, but it is far from proof of anti-clientelist governance. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.5

- **[The Moscow Times designated a foreign agent](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-designates-the-moscow-times-newspaper-a-foreign-agent-3238256)** | *Reuters* | Nov. 18, 2023 | The Justice Ministry imposed new disclosure burdens on an already blocked independent outlet. That is administrative pressure on independent information rather than even-handed treatment. | **Questions:** 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.8

**Search Gap**
- I did not find credible 2023 evidence that Putin generally avoided patronage in pardons or procurement.
- The strongest positive material is limited to standardized social benefits and a few technocratic economic interventions.
- The dominant 2023 pattern is favoring loyalists, punishing scrutiny, and using state power transactionally in appointments, enforcement, property control, and information access.
